paper.title_en: QCD Crossover Transfer Functions for Scalar-Induced Gravitational Waves in the PTA Band
paper.abstract_en: Pulsar timing array (PTA) collaborations have reported evidence for a stochastic gravitational wave (GW) background in the nHz band. Should scalar-induced GWs, sourced at second order by enhanced primordial curvature perturbations, contribute to this signal, a coincidence of scales makes them directly sensitive to the softening of the equation of state around the QCD crossover. We solve the tensor and scalar equations of motion across the Standard Model (SM) thermal history and tabulate the transfer functions for direct use in present and future PTA analyses. We show that this SM effect modifies the height of the induced spectrum by up to $\approx55\%$ across the PTA band relative to the radiation-domination expectation, with either sign depending on whether the source modes cross the horizon before or after the crossover. Fitting the NANOGrav 15-year data with a broken-power-law curvature power spectrum, we find that including the crossover shifts the inferred peak amplitude and scale by an amount that could already be relevant for the comparison with primordial black hole overproduction bounds. The importance of this SM effect will grow as the statistical uncertainty on the amplitude and scale shrinks with future, more sensitive PTA datasets, at which point neglecting it could significantly bias the inference.

decision.selection_reason_zh: 该文直接面向PTA频段的标量诱导引力波，计算了QCD交叉期间标准模型热历史对张量与标量运动方程的转移函数，并给出对NANOGrav 15年数据的拟合影响及与PBH过量产生界限的比较，属于PTA相关的高理论深度研究，方法明确（数值求解与表格化转移函数），对后续PTA分析有直接的可复用价值。
decision.title_zh: PTA频段中标量诱导引力波的QCD交叉转移函数
decision.abstract_zh: 脉冲星计时阵列（PTA）合作组已报告了nHz频段随机引力波（GW）背景的证据。若由增强的原初曲率扰动二阶产生的标量诱导引力波对该信号有贡献，则尺度的巧合使它们直接对QCD交叉附近状态方程的软化敏感。我们在标准模型（SM）热历史中求解张量和标量运动方程，并制表给出转移函数，以供当前和未来PTA分析直接使用。我们表明，相对于辐射主导预期，这一SM效应在PTA频段上将诱导谱的高度改变最多约55\%，其符号取决于源模是在交叉之前还是之后穿越视界。用破幂律曲率功率谱拟合NANOGrav 15年数据，我们发现纳入交叉会使推断的峰值振幅和尺度发生移动，该移动量可能已经与对原初黑洞过量产生界限的比较相关。随着未来更灵敏的PTA数据集使振幅和尺度的统计不确定度缩小，这一SM效应的重要性将会增长，届时忽略它可能显著偏置推断。
